key_insight: MCTS can waste exploration on differently worded versions of the same reasoning strategy; learned pseudo-counts let related branches share exploration evidence.
engineering_relevance: Changing only UCT’s exploration statistic offers a targeted way to improve LLM reasoning search without redesigning the full search algorithm.
method: Identify count fragmentation caused by assigning independent visit counts to textual branches.
Use a lightweight Coin-Flipping Network head on policy hidden representations to estimate representation coverage.
Replace standard UCT exploration counts with learned pseudo-counts in LPC-MCTS.
evidence_signal: Across 5 math and 7 search benchmarks, LPC-MCTS outperformed strong MCTS baselines; inference-only count replacement with fixed LPC-MCTS-trained policies improved average mean@16 math accuracy by 3.79 percentage points on Qwen2.5-7B and 2.71 on Qwen3-4B.
watch_item: The reported inference-only gains use LPC-MCTS-trained policies, so they do not establish equivalent gains from a drop-in replacement on arbitrary pretrained policies.
paper_title: MCTS Is Counting the Wrong Thing: Learning Exploration Counts for LLM Reasoning
